- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price dip is sharp.
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward prior 10-day average, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is weak or mixed, model often underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 18-day price is trending down.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model may overreact; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or next 3-day average confirms trend.
